newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries steady at midday, Fed bought coupons.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries steady at midday, Fed bought coupons.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices were steady at higher levels on Wednesday, aided by a steady dollar, the Federal Reserve's coupon purchases, and expectations for subdued reports on May retail sales and wholesale price, analysts said.

"We're firm because the dollar has been able to hold its own, particularly against the European Continental currencies," said William Sullivan, senior vice president and director of fixed-income research at Dean Witter Reynolds.
At noon EDT/1600 GMT, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 6/32 to 97-14/32, yielding 6.83 percent. In early dealings, the 30-year bond was up 5/32.
Sullivan said the Fed's decision to add permanent reserves to the banking system by buying coupons was mildly surprising and another positive factor for prices.

"Most analysts were forecasting permanent reserve provisions but were looking more for a bill pass," he said. "The Fed is removing some supply from dealers' shelves that was not fully allowed for so that has been a supporting influence as well."

Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc., said the fact that the Treasury market held its own after the dollar weakened overnight "suggests a generally positive and resilient tone" in the market.
"Most people would have expected the market to be off early today based on what the dollar did overnight," he said.
The dollar slid below 111 yen overnight.

Analysts said the market might also be reflecting a little relief after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech in New York on Tuesday night did not offer any hints as to the direction of U.S. monetary policy.
"Knowing that in the past the Chairman has delivered hints about monetary policy, there may be some relief that there was nothing in the Greenspan speech that would hurt the market," said Moran.

"The fundamentals that have been propelling prices higher are still in place, there has been no further news on the EMU arrangement and there were no damaging statements from Greenspan," he said. "That, plus the coupon pass has kept (Treasury prices) in the plus column."

The near-term fundamental influences that are expected to be friendly to the inflation-wary credit markets are the May U.S. retail sales report due on Thursday and the Producer Price Index (PPI) report due on Friday.
Retail sales are expected to be up just modestly after declining in April. The PPI is forcast to be up 0.1 percent.
At midday, three-month bill rates were down four basis points to 4.86 percent. Six-month and year-bill rates were each down one basis point to 5.19 percent and 5.42 percent, respectively.

Two-year notes were up 1/32 to 100-6/32, yielding 6.15 percent. Five-year notes were priced at 100-8/32 to yield 6.44 percent. Ten-year notes were trading at 100-17/32, up 4/32, to yield 6.55 percent.
